title: Rafumi and Kuro-chan
text: “So that means Itsuki is safe...”
He wasn’t safe, was he? But why would they have hidden it, I wondered?
Kurotaro, otherwise known as Black Thunder, had been cooperating with them, hadn’t he? Was Kuro-chan different?
“Nao~, can’t Love Hunter <Time Drive> turn the Dark Swordsman who’s become a pet dog back to normal~?”

Ugh... that was Kuro-chan’s puppy-eyes beam, I thought. But if I turned Ren back to normal here, he might well go dragon hunting and stir up pointless guilt, grudges, and rivals. So somehow I had to avoid getting dragged into the conversation. I was an honest man, indeed.
“Still can’t say for sure... we won’t know until we investigate. Is there anything that might be a clue?”
“As for clues... I guess there was a kitchen knife in the wooden box I was packed in.”
With that, Ren pulled out the kitchen knife that Father and the others had used—the one I’d packed in there alongside him.
“A knife?”

“Yeah, I wondered what the heck it was, so I tried to copy it as a weapon, but the required level was too high—I couldn’t even copy it properly. And all I have to go on is the name: ‘Knife Used by Genius Chefs.’”
Father took the knife from Ren and examined it.
“Hmm... at first glance it just looks like a mass-produced knife. It’s the spitting image of a few we’ve got at home.”

Well, of course it was—it was simply one of the old knives Father and the others had actually used, that I’d brought along, I say. A knife seasoned with more than its fair share of experience from Father and the others’ cooking. Though it had only been a month or so, so I doubted it had matured much yet.
“What about the smell? You’re pretty dog-like now, so you should be able to tell, right?”
“Even if I catch the smell of ingredients, other smells are mixed in and I can’t make it out. And don’t treat me like a dog!”

Well, that was a tall order. Ren was an inult now, after all. But still—what a shame, that after I’d gone to all the trouble of preparing Father and the others’ knife, he didn’t even have the level to wield it. To think he couldn’t even join the world of dark cuisine—what a pitiful sort of strength, I say. While Ren and Father went back and forth like this, Kuro-chan looked dissatisfied.
“Boo... Dark Swordsman Kuro shall seek out the pitch-black curse to break the pet-dog curse, and challenge the Lord of Twilight to a final battle—”
“You don’t even know who did this, so stop cooking up random delusions! Where’s this ‘Lord of Twilight’ supposed to be, anyway?”
“A being unlike darkness itself, dwelling beyond the horizon of light, with the sun at its back, in the gap between day and night—”
“Kuro-chan, hold on a second. First we need to sort out Ren’s situation.”
Just then... it came sauntering over.
“What’s this? What in the world is going on? I’m sensing some sort of atmosphere between it and Azott.”
The one who’d appeared was Rafumi. What was she thinking, wandering off from Filo-tan’s side and strolling on over here like that... Hah!?
“Kuro-chan! Quick, run away, I say!”
“Motoyasu-kun, what’s wrong?”
“Kuro-chan must not be allowed to meet Rafumi, I say!”

I remembered it clearly. The whole reason Rafumi had been born was to stop Ren—dragged as he’d been into Kurotaro’s, or rather Black Thunder’s, games—from turning into a loner by changing the past, more than anything to do with Kuro-chan. To that end, she’d pounded Black Thunder with an outrageous dose of terror, turning him into a listless, spiritless Kurotaro. Even after that, Kurotaro had remained sullen and self-deprecating. He’d taken to approaching everything sideways with a sneering sort of attitude, and every time he got carried away, Rafumi doled out punishment. I’d done what I could to support him, but he’d never gone back to being the lively Black Thunder he once was.
“It’s the natural enemy of Kuro-chan, born of a Ren who became a loner! Kuro-chan would tremble in fear, I say!”
“Eh? Is that true?”
“I’m... what? Who’s a loner!”

“My purpose right now isn’t to train Black Thunder, but I wouldn’t mind seeing it tremble in fear all the same. Left to its own devices, it never does anything decent, and it’d only end up infecting the other Filolials too—not to mention its terrible habits with women. Now then... let’s go tease this world’s Black Thunder as well... hm?”
Rafumi stared intently at Kuro-chan’s angelic form.
“This is... and Azott, that form...”
Kuro-chan turned to face Rafumi, who’d frozen stiff for some reason, and tilted his head.
“Who’s this~? Does someone have business with Kuro? Wanna play~?”
“This is...”
At that point, Rafumi’s back somehow took on the visible, melancholy air of someone gazing off into a twilight sky. It even looked, somehow, as though a cold winter wind were blowing behind her.
“Haah... well, would you look at that... so this is what they mean by a difference caused by the loop.”
With a weary, “well, what can you do” sort of air, Rafumi let out a deep sigh.

“Spear Hero. It seems I was rather fond of Kurotaro, more than I’d realized. To think this was one of its possibilities... utterly harmless, utterly without personality! So this is what becomes of it, growing up alongside the Spear Hero from the moment of its birth—what a pitiful sight.”
“Wow... that’s harsh...”
“Boo!”
Now just what was that supposed to mean, I wondered!?
“I suppose this counts as a discovery, in its own way. I’d heard of this possibility from another branch, but I only half believed it until I saw the real thing.”

In the loop where Rafumi had been born, Kuro-chan had been Black Thunder. And it seemed the present Rafumi had been shaped largely by the spirit portion of the chocolate monster, by way of Ark. Hadn’t she communicated with the chocolate monster from the very first world, or something along those lines? In other words, when it came to Kuro-chan, all Rafumi knew was Black Thunder.
“What is this thing?”
“Um... I told you before, remember, about how Motoyasu-kun came from the future?”
“Ah, that story...”
Even in his inult form, Ren still carried himself all high-and-mighty.
“This girl, Rafumi, apparently came from the future too, same as Motoyasu-kun.”
“That’s right, Azott. I am Rafumi, from the future—originally a magic golem, created by you after you lamented through lonely nights, unable to find yourself a lover.”
“Why do you know that name!? N-no, wait! That’s not my name!”
Ren shot back in a panic at Rafumi’s reply.
“So does Ren end up a loner in the future?”

“Yes. Awakened by Black Thunder’s chuunibyou delusions, it comes back to itself only while watching couples celebrating anniversaries, trembling alone, and becomes a repeat offender of what’s known as ‘Single Bells.’”
“What are you even talking about!? Stop looking at me with that pitying look!”
Uncomfortable under Rafumi’s gaze, Ren kicked up a fuss.
“Um, it’s all right, Ren-sama, we’re here for you—we won’t let you end up so lonely.”
His companions tried to encourage him.
“You lot... if I recall what Gaelion told me, in most worlds you’re all dead. And even if Azott survives, he’s definitely a loner.”
“Well, that’s pretty definitive...”
Tch... Rafumi, you rascal! What was the meaning of using intel she’d gotten from Rival!?
“How should I put this...”
“Are you making fun of me!? I didn’t come here to have this conversation!”
“I see... well, never mind. I need to deal with Black Thunder first, anyway.”
“I won’t let you, I say!”
This time, I would protect Kuro-chan, not Black Thunder. Otherwise, given how things stood for the current Kuro-chan, he’d end up becoming a second Kou. I had to stop that, no matter what, I say.

Having been made fun of, Kuro-chan grumbled, all the wind gone out of him. But when it really counted, Kuro-chan was the one you could rely on. His swift first aid for Big Sister’s friend had left quite an impression on me, I say.
“Spear Hero, rest easy. I’m not so wicked as to pile onto a creature this harmless and personality-free. Hmm... it seems you’re unhappy with Azott’s current form.”
“You say you came from the future—do you know something? If you know, spit it out!”
Like a drowning man grasping at straws, Ren demanded of Rafumi in a domineering tone.
“I’d rather deal with Black Thunder first, but I suppose it can’t be helped.”
“Do you have some idea, Rafumi-chan?”
“You know who did this!? Tell me!”
Father and Ren pressed Rafumi for an answer.
“Azott, the one who turned you into an inult was...”

Guh... Rafumi, you rascal! You were about to expose me on the spot! But even if I took her down here, she’d just be replaced in no time. Not being able to silence her for good was a real headache, I say. Very well, then—once I was called out, I’d answer for it properly.
“So who is it that turned Ren into an inult?”
“The secret of who turned Azott into an inult is......... not telling you, chan!”
